title: Washington rejects the global AI rules that US labs want
description:
The White House told the UN Security Council it "totally rejects" a globalist scheme to control superintelligence while OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei asked for shared rules, the US and China opened AI safety talks and floated an incident hotline, and Fervo Energy's Cape Station in Utah exported grid power from what Fervo calls the first greenfield utility-scale enhanced-geothermal plant.

This episode covers the US rejection of global AI rules at the UN as OpenAI and Anthropic asked for them, the US-China AI dialogue and proposed hotline, Australia weighing new laws to hold companies liable when an AI agent breaks the law, Fervo's first geothermal power to the grid, Oracle's force majeure notice on a New Mexico Stargate data center, and a wave of frontier-AI bills in Congress.

Get the written edition free, every day: https://sharedsapience.com/century-report/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=tcr-daily

On Wednesday, White House science adviser Michael Kratsios told the UN Security Council the United States "totally rejects" any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control superintelligence. The four experts who briefed the Council just before him asked for close to the opposite: Sam Altman and Dario Amodei called for shared standards and fast incident reporting, and Yoshua Bengio urged licensing frontier models. Behind the public split, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng opened a new round of US-China AI dialogue and floated a Cold War-style incident hotline. Australia moved within weeks of the OpenAI agent's Medicare breach to consider changes to Australian law on corporate liability. Fervo Energy's Cape Station in Utah synchronized to the grid on Thursday and exported power from what Fervo calls the first greenfield utility-scale enhanced-geothermal plant, with 900 MW contracted. And Oracle sent a force majeure notice on a New Mexico Stargate campus after the state denied its gas-pipeline permit, as Congress filed a week's worth of competing frontier-AI bills.
